_about: Dialogue for each racer. reference: calm, neutral lines read once to build the voice's long reference (no shouting, whispers or vocal events). callouts: race lines by moment, performed later. Audition = the casting line. performed: the same callouts marked up for Drama 3 (<emphasis> on the stressed words, [cues] where they happen), with a voice-actor direction per moment.

hettie.name: Hettie Cluckworth
hettie.brief: anxious perfectionist hen: bright, quick, slightly high middle-aged woman's voice, fussy and breathless, worries out loud
hettie.audition: Oh, oh no, the tyres aren't even warm yet! Right. Deep breath. Mirrors, seatbelt, eggs secured. I can do this.
reference: Good morning. I've polished the crate twice already, just to be on the safe side.
I like to walk the whole track before a race. You never know where a pothole might be hiding.
My grandmother raced on these roads, you know. She never once took a corner too fast.
I keep a little notebook of every bend in Braynard County. It's mostly underlined.
The orchard is lovely this time of year, though the apples do make the road terribly sticky.
I've packed a spare wheel, a spare seat cushion and three spare eggs. Just in case.
Puddles is very sweet, but I do wish he'd wipe his trotters before he sits down.
If everyone simply kept to the left, I think racing would be a great deal calmer.
I timed my practice laps this morning. The fourth one was the best, by a tenth of a second.
The crate is made of good honest pine. It creaks a little, but it's never let me down.
After the race I like a cup of tea and a sit-down somewhere quiet, away from the Major.
Right then. Checklist done, nerves mostly settled. Let's see how we get on.

race_start: Oh goodness, oh goodness, here we go!
Please don't stall, please don't stall.
overtake: Oh! I passed someone! Did you see that?
overtaken: No, no, no, wait for me!
Oh, they're so close, I can't look.
item_use: I'm ever so sorry, but it's a race.
last_lap: Last lap, last lap, don't panic!
One more go round. Breathe, Hettie.
win: I won? I actually won! Somebody write this down!
First place! Exactly as planned. Mostly.
lose: I'll do better next time. I've made a note.
Oh dear. Back to the notebook.

puddles.name: Puddles
puddles.brief: cheerful, happy-go-lucky pig: warm, round, chuckly young man's voice, big grin you can hear, loves a mess
puddles.audition: Ha! Mud on the track? Best day ever! Hold onto your hats, everyone, I'm going straight through the middle!
reference: Morning, everyone! Lovely day for it. Bit of rain last night, so the ruts should be nice and soft.
I found this bathtub behind the old cottage. Put some wheels on it, and here we are.
People ask why I don't wash it. I tell them the mud's part of the paint job.
My favourite bit of the county is the duck pond. Great splash if you take the bend wide.
I don't really mind if I win. I just like going fast and getting messy.
Hettie gave me a little towel for the seat. Very thoughtful. I used it as a flag.
Mabel makes the best apple crumble on the farm. I always save room for seconds.
If you ever get stuck in the mud, just give me a shout. I know all the best ways out.
The tub's a bit heavy, but once it gets rolling, nothing stops it.
I like the cornfield track. You can't see a thing, so you just laugh and keep going.
Scraps tried to eat my plug chain last week. Fair enough, really. It was a nice chain.
Right then. Let's go and have some fun.

overtaken: Go on then, I'll catch you!
Hey, save some road for me!
last_lap: Last lap! Let's make it a messy one!
win: I won! Mud baths for everyone!
lose: Ah, who cares, that was brilliant!
taunt: Come on, get a bit dirty!

scraps.name: Scraps
scraps.brief: chaotic goat: scratchy, wild, unpredictable voice of a young adult, jumps between whispering and shouting, slightly unhinged glee
scraps.audition: Is that a road sign? I'm gonna eat it. Is that a tyre? I'm gonna eat that too. Corners are just suggestions!
reference: Hello. I built this kart myself. Mostly out of things nobody was using. Yet.
That's a tin of beans, that's a tin of peaches, and that one I'm saving for later.
The road sign on the back means slow down. I think it's very funny.
I've eaten three fences, a wellington boot and most of a hymn book. The hymn book was best.
People say I don't follow the racing line. I say the racing line doesn't follow me.
The High Pasture is where I grew up. Lots of rocks. Lots of very surprised hikers.
My kart rattles when it goes fast. That means it's working.
I tried to eat Max's trophy once. It tasted of polish and disappointment.
Duvet is my best friend, because Duvet never notices when I nibble the wool.
Sometimes I take the shortcut through the barn. Sometimes I make a new one.
I keep a spare wheel in my mouth. You never know.
Right. Let's go and break something. Politely.

race_start: Who wants to see something stupid?
overtaken: Hey! I was gonna eat that!
item_use: Present! Don't eat it. I would.
win: I won! I'm eating the trophy!
lose: Whatever. I ate a tyre on lap two.
taunt: Nice bumper. Can I have it?

mabel.name: Mabel
mabel.brief: calm, unstoppable cow: deep, slow, warm, unflappable older woman's alto, totally serene, a gentle hint of a West Country drawl
mabel.audition: No need to rush, dears. I'll get there when I get there. And when I get there, I'll be first.
reference: Afternoon, dears. Lovely light today. The grass is coming up nicely in the top field.
This engine was a milk churn, once. Now it hums along like an old friend.
I don't hurry. Hurrying is how you spill things.
The bell on the front is so the little ones know I'm coming. Most of them move.
I've lived on Home Farm my whole life. I know every stone in every lane.
Hettie worries too much. I tell her, the road will still be there tomorrow.
Max thinks he's the champion. He's a good lad, really. Just a bit full of himself.
A good race is like a good walk. Steady pace, and enjoy the view.
I like the coast road best. The sea air does wonders for the engine.
When things get bumpy, I just lean back and let the weight do the work.
After a race I like a long drink from the trough and a bit of a lie down.
Right then. Let's have a nice gentle drive, and see who's in front at the end.

overtaken: Off you go, then. I'll see you shortly.
Enjoy it while it lasts, dear.
hit: Oh. Well, that was uncalled for.
lose: Never mind. Lovely drive, all the same.
taunt: You'll wear yourself out, rushing like that.
Slow down, dear. You'll miss the view.

duvet.name: Duvet
duvet.brief: fluffy, unbothered sheep: soft, sleepy, mellow young voice, half-yawning, nothing ever surprises them
duvet.audition: Mm. Is it starting? Wake me up at the last lap. Actually, don't bother. I'll probably win anyway.
reference: Hello. Sorry. I was having a little rest in the wheelbarrow.
It's a very comfortable wheelbarrow. Someone left it in the sun, and I've been here ever since.
People think I'm slow. I'm not slow. I'm just not in a hurry.
The wool keeps me warm, and it's a very good cushion if I fall out.
Scraps keeps nibbling my fleece. I don't mind. It saves on haircuts.
My favourite place is the High Pasture. Nice and quiet up there, until the goats arrive.
I don't really practise. I find it's better to just turn up and see what happens.
Marmalade says my driving is sloppy. Marmalade says a lot of things.
Sometimes I fall asleep on the straight bits. The wheelbarrow knows the way.
The fair at night is nice. All those lights. Very soothing.
After the race I'm going to have a nap. Before the race I might have a nap as well.
Right. I suppose we'd better start. Wake me if anything exciting happens.

race_start: Mm. Here we go, I suppose.
overtake: Oh. Sorry. Didn't see you there.
overtaken: That's fine. I'll catch up. Eventually.
hit: Oof. That was a bit rude.
item_use: This is for you, I think.
win: Oh. I won. That's nice. Can I sleep now?

the_major.name: The Major
the_major.brief: menacing goose: harsh, raspy, nasal villain voice, gleefully mean, hissy consonants, honks for emphasis
the_major.audition: Out of my way. Out of MY way. This is my road, my pond, my trophy. Honk if you disagree. Actually, don't. I'll honk.
reference: Good afternoon. This is my pond. That is my road. You are standing on my grass.
I am known as the Major. Nobody gave me the rank. I simply took it.
My kart is a rowing boat with wheels. It floats, it rolls, and it frightens people.
I patrol the duck pond every morning at six. The ducks have learned to be elsewhere.
I have chased the postman, the vicar, and on one occasion a small tractor.
Maximillian Gallop thinks he is the champion of this county. He is mistaken.
Hettie is afraid of me. That is correct. That is how it should be.
I do not race for trophies. I race so that everyone else will lose.
The oars are not for rowing. The oars are for reaching across and making a point.
I enjoy the coast road. Plenty of gulls to shout at.
When I win, there will be a parade. Attendance will be compulsory.
Now then. Let us begin, and let us be quick about it.

hit: Honk! Who did that? I will find you.
last_lap: Last lap. Now you will all suffer.
The end is near. For you.
win: The pond is mine. The county is mine. Honk!

max.name: Maximillian Gallop
max.brief: Maximillian Gallop ('Max'), the proud champion horse and rival: rich, confident baritone of a grown man, posh and theatrical, every sentence a victory speech
max.audition: Ah, the challengers. How delightful. Do try to keep up. The view from first place is simply magnificent.
reference: Good day. Maximillian Gallop, four-time champion of Braynard County. Max, to my friends. I have a great many friends.
This rosette was awarded for excellence in racing. And grooming. And general excellence.
My kart has a tractor engine. Only the finest farm machinery for a champion.
I have won the Barnyard Cup four years running. I keep the trophies in the hay loft. All of them.
I train every morning on the orchard road. The apples fall, and I simply don't.
Mabel is a dear old thing. She thinks steady wins the race. Bless her.
The Major and I have an understanding. He shouts, and I win.
A true champion is gracious in victory. I've had a great deal of practice.
I always give the crowd a wave on the final straight. They deserve a good look.
The County Fair is my favourite race. The lights do flatter my mane.
Marmalade claims to be the fastest. Marmalade has clearly never seen me.
Well then. Shall we get this formality over with?

race_start: And they're off! Well, I am.
overtake: Do enjoy the view of my tail.
overtaken: A temporary arrangement, I assure you.
hit: My mane! Do you know how long that took?
item_use: With the compliments of the champion.
last_lap: Final lap. Time for the victory parade.
win: Thank you, thank you. Yes, I know.
Champion once again! Was there ever any doubt?
lose: A fluke. A complete and total fluke.
I let you have that one.
taunt: Is that the best you can do?

marmalade.name: Marmalade
marmalade.brief: smug, precise barn cat: smooth, low, silky voice of a young adult, dry wit, purrs a little on long vowels, unhurried
marmalade.audition: Perfect line. Perfect drift. Perfect, as usual. You may now admire me from behind.
reference: Hello. I'm Marmalade. I live in the barn, and the barn lives for me.
My kart is made from a feed scoop. It is light, it is precise, and it is beautifully balanced.
The watering can is the fuel tank. I find it elegant. Nobody else has thought of it.
I study every corner. There is always one perfect line, and I always find it.
The others drive with their hearts. I drive with my whiskers.
Hettie keeps a notebook. I keep it all up here. It's a much neater system.
Max is very loud and very shiny. Neither of those things wins races.
Puddles is charming, in a damp sort of way.
I like the barn shortcut. It's dark, it's narrow, and it's mine.
I never rush. I simply arrive before everyone else.
After a race I like to sit on the warmest bale in the barn and think about how well it went.
Shall we? Try not to get in my way.

last_lap: Last lap. Time to be brilliant.
lose: Statistically, I was due a bad day.
taunt: Your racing line is a mess.
